## Tokyo 5-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg

A balanced Tokyo plan for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-15** with **food, museums, one day trip, mid-range hotels, and easy train access**.
Budget target: **$2,800 total excluding international flights**; I’m assuming this covers hotel, local transit, food, admissions, and the day trip.

## Day-by-Day Itinerary and Spending
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Day | Area focus | Plan | Est. spend (JPY) | Est. spend (USD) |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Day 1 | Ueno + Asakusa | Arrive, check in, Ueno Park, Tokyo National Museum, Asakusa dinner | ¥26,000 | $173 |
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/2014_02_08_ueno.jpg Alt=| Day 1 | Ueno + Asakusa | Arrive, check in, Ueno Park, Tokyo National Museum, Asakusa dinner | ¥26,000 | $173 |, Tokyo, Japan
| Day 2 | Shinjuku + Shibuya | Meiji Jingu, teamLab/modern museum option, Shibuya food crawl, skyline stop | ¥30,000 | $200 |
| Day 3 | Central Tokyo | Imperial Palace area, Tokyo Station, museum or gallery, Ginza dining | ¥28,000 | $187 |
| Day 4 | Day trip | Nikko or Kamakura day trip with temples, local lunch, return to Tokyo | ¥36,000 | $240 |
Media: Alt=| Day 4 | Day trip | Nikko or Kamakura day trip with temples, local lunch, return to Tokyo | ¥36,000 | $240 |, Tokyo, Japan
| Day 5 | Odaiba + Tokyo Bay | Miraikan or art museum, waterfront walk, final sushi/ramen dinner | ¥27,000 | $180 |
Media: Alt=| Day 5 | Odaiba + Tokyo Bay | Miraikan or art museum, waterfront walk, final sushi/ramen dinner | ¥27,000 | $180 |, Tokyo, Japan

**Trip total estimate:** **¥147,000** to **¥165,000** for 2 adults, roughly **$980 to $1,100** at typical exchange rates.
That leaves room inside your **$2,800** budget for a stronger hotel, more dining upgrades, or shopping.

### Day 1: Ueno + Asakusa Arrival Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive, transfer to hotel, light lunch near Ueno or Asakusa.
- Afternoon: **Tokyo National Museum** and a relaxed walk through **Ueno Park**.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: **Tokyo National Museum** and a relaxed walk through **Ueno Park**, Tokyo, Japan
- Evening: Explore **Senso-ji** area, then dinner on **Nakamise-dori** or nearby streets.
- Food: Tempura, soba, or a casual izakaya near Asakusa.
- Transit logic: Stay in **Ueno/Asakusa** so your first day is simple after arrival.

### Day 2: Shinjuku + Shibuya Museums and City Energy
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: **Meiji Jingu** and Yoyogi area for a calm start.
- Afternoon: Choose one museum-style stop such as **teamLab Planets**, **Mori Art Museum**, or a design/gallery visit.
- Evening: Shibuya crossing, dinner, and a short observatory or rooftop stop.
- Food: Ramen lunch, then yakitori or modern Japanese dinner.
- Transit logic: Keep the day on the **Yamanote Line west side** to reduce backtracking.

### Day 3: Central Tokyo Cultural Loop
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: **Imperial Palace East Gardens** or nearby heritage walk.
- Afternoon: **Tokyo Station / Marunouchi** area, then one museum or specialty exhibit.
- Evening: **Ginza** for a nicer dinner and dessert stop.
- Food: Sushi set lunch or kaiseki-style dinner if you want one splurge meal.
- Transit logic: This cluster works well because **Tokyo, Otemachi, and Ginza** are tightly connected.

### Day 4: One Day Trip Outside Tokyo
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Leave early for **Nikko** if you want temples and nature, or **Kamakura** if you want a lighter, easier day.
- Afternoon: Temples, shrine areas, local lunch, and scenic walking.
- Evening: Return to Tokyo for a simple dinner near your hotel.
- Food: Try local specialty noodles or a set meal near the station.
- Transit logic: Pick **one destination only** and use the station area as your base all day.

### Day 5: Odaiba + Tokyo Bay Farewell
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: **Miraikan** or another modern museum in Odaiba.
- Afternoon: Waterfront walk, shopping, and relaxed café time.
- Evening: Final dinner with a view or a polished sushi meal.
- Food: Seafood bowl, sushi, or a final comfort meal before departure.
- Transit logic: Odaiba is best done as a **single cluster day** with no cross-city detours.

## Hotel Area Strategy for Easy Train Access
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

| Area | Why it works | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| **Ueno** | Direct airport access, strong rail links, good value | First/last nights, museum access |
| **Shinjuku** | Huge transit hub, many hotel choices, easy day-trip departures | Nightlife, day-trip flexibility |
| **Tokyo Station / Marunouchi** | Fast access across the city, polished mid-range hotels | Central sightseeing, business-style comfort |
| **Asakusa** | Good value, easy sightseeing, calmer evenings | Traditional Tokyo feel, lower hotel cost |

**Best fit for your trip:**
- **Primary choice: Ueno or Tokyo Station area**
- **Best value choice: Asakusa**
- **Best transit convenience: Shinjuku**

## Transit-Minimizing Grouping Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg

- Group **Ueno + Asakusa** together for temples, museums, and the arrival day.
- Group **Shinjuku + Shibuya + Meiji Jingu** together on one west-side day.
- Group **Tokyo Station + Ginza + Imperial Palace** together in central Tokyo.
- Put **Odaiba** on its own day because it is a separate bay-area cluster.
- Use the **day trip** as its own full-day block so it does not fragment the rest of the itinerary.
